first_boot.note: includes image pull; not a resume measurement

method.driver: RunPod REST v2 via MCP (POST /pods/{id}/action stop|start), the same calls scripts/anchors/anchorctl.py measure makes
method.stop_seconds: stop action responses returned status=EXITED synchronously; recorded as 1s
method.resume_ready_seconds: start-issue wall clock to runtime-ready, where ready = poll_time minus the runtime.uptime counter in the first poll that showed a non-null runtime; polls at 20-30s intervals, so ready is back-computed, not poll-bounded
not_verified: SSH-level reachability (outbound SSH blocked from the measuring sandbox)

container-disk persistence across stop: RunPod documents the container disk as ephemeral across stop/start with only volumes persisting; this pod has NO volume, so node identity would not survive a stop. Recreation with a /workspace volume is pending owner approval.

observations.identity_across_resume: same pod id and public IP across all three resumes; ephemeral SSH port changed each time (22139 -> 22081 -> 22142 -> 22182)
observations.stopped_billing: disk-only while stopped (published rate, modelled ~USD 0.008/hr for 30 GiB; reconcile against invoice before quoting)
